items.title: ROAD CLOSED: Pedestrian killed in Mississauga crash
items.summary: Last Updated September 29, 2026 at 7:38 pm One person is dead and police have closed a busy street following a crash in Mississauga. m. in the area of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West, Peel Regional Police say. A pedestrian was struck by a vehicle and was pronounced dead at the scene. No details about the victim have been disclosed by police, but a spokesperson with Peel Regional Paramedic Services has confirmed the victim was an adult. Police have closed all eastbound and westbound lanes on Dundas Street between at Hampshire Gate through the intersection of Winston Churchill to Woodchester Drive. Drivers in the area should expect delays, and police say motorists are advised to avoid the area while emergency crews are on the scene. Anyone with information about this incident can contact Peel Regional Police by calling 905-453-3311. ca.

items.title: AI data centre task force formed to keep Mississauga residents in the loop
items.summary: The city has struck a new task force intended to keep Mississauga residents informed as a study on the impact of AI data centres is completed. A Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force that includes City of Mississauga councillors, city planning staff, industry stakeholders and members of the public was approved Tuesday at city council. The temporary body will, among other functions, provide “regular updates” on a comprehensive review being conducted by senior city staff. They’re looking into the large data centres and any new rules coming from the provincial government that would regulate the rapidly growing industry. “Transparent reporting for the benefit of the public” will also be provided by the new task force, which was called for in a motion brought forth this week by Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden. Council moves to halt buiding of new data centres The green light for the task force comes two weeks after city council approved an interim control bylaw that halted the building of large data centres in Mississauga for at least one year. City of Mississauga councillors were unanimous in their support of the temporary bylaw that imposes a moratorium of one year — and up to two years — on data centre developments in Mississauga. Pausing such developments will allow the city more time to study the matter and any new rules that would regulate the rapidly growing industry. S. as well.

items.title: Election signs aren’t allowed on public property
items.summary: City crews are proactively patrolling the city and removing illegally placed signs, and residents can contact the city to report an illegal sign. Campaigns will be charged a $20 per day, per sign fee for the City to store illegal signs, if they do not follow the Sign By-law. As Election signs are starting to appear across Mississauga as part of the municipal election scheduled for October 26, the City is reminding residents and candidates about the rules for election signs and how residents can report concerns. Election signs are a common part of election campaigns and are permitted in Mississauga if they follow the City’s Sign By-law. Election signs do not need a permit. These rules help keep roads, sidewalks and public spaces safe. They also help prevent visibility problems and other hazards. Residents who believe an election sign does not follow the Sign By-law, can report it through the City’s online service form or call 311. Residents are asked to not remove or move election signs on public property, but to contact the City. Property owners may remove election signs from their own property if they did not give permission for the sign to be placed there. City staff will review each report of an illegal sign. If a sign does not follow the by-law, the City may remove it and may take further enforcement action, including laying charges under the Provincial Offences Act. City crews are also proactively patrolling the city and will remove illegally placed signs.

items.title: Inquest into death of man killed during interaction with police in Mississauga set to start
items.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Mississauga man killed seven years ago during an interaction with police is scheduled to begin in three weeks, the province said Tuesday. Dr. Richard Wells, regional supervising coroner for the Central Region Toronto West Office, announced the inquest, which will look into the Sept. 10, 2019 death of Matthew DiGiovanni, 34, will get underway on Oct. m. The proceedings, which will be conducted by video conference, are expected to last 10 days and hear from approximately 12 witnesses. Dr. John Carlisle will be the presiding officer and Peter Napier will be the inquest counsel, the province’s ministry of the solicitor general said in a news release. DiGiovanni died shortly after being shot with a Taser wielded by Peel Regional Police at his family’s home in the Malton area of Mississauga. The inquest into DiGiovanni’s death is mandatory under the Coroners Act, the province said earlier. “The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Mr. DiGiovanni’s death. The jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing further deaths,” the release stated. An inquest is a public hearing conducted by a coroner, lawyer or retired judge before a jury of five community members.

items.title: What’s open, closed in Mississauga for Wednesday’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
items.summary: Most retail stores are open Sept. 30 as National Day for Truth and Reconciliation is not a statutory holiday in Ontario. Most City of Mississauga services are closed Wednesday, Sept. 30 for National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. On Sept. 30, 2013 Orange Shirt Day — Every Child Matters began as a grassroots movement in Williams Lake, BC to honour Residential School survivors, their families and those who never returned home. The National Day for Truth and Reconciliation was a response to Call to Action 80 of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. It called on the federal government, in partnership with Indigenous communities to create a statutory holiday which recognizes survivors, their communities and families, while ensuring the history and legacy of residential schools is remembered publicly. Since June 3, 2021, National Day for Truth and Reconciliation is marked as a federal statutory holiday. Hours for various service vary. Here’s what’s open and closed on Sept. 30. items.title: Crown Electric Launches Commercial EV Charger Installation in Mississauga
items.summary: Crown Electric Ltd, a licensed Ontario electrical contractor, now offers commercial EV charger installation for Mississauga property owners, covering permitting, panel assessments and code-compliant setup for retail, hospitality and office sites. Oakville, Canada, September 29, 2026 -- Crown Electric Ltd, a licensed Ontario electrical contractor serving Oakville, Mississauga, Burlington and Etobicoke, has announced commercial EV charger installation services for property owners in Mississauga. The new offering gives retail, hospitality and office landlords a way to add EV charging infrastructure through a code-compliant provider with decades of experience serving the region. ca/commercial-electrician-mississauga/. The timing reflects a shift in how drivers choose where to shop and dine, as charging availability increasingly factors into these decisions and turns EV chargers into a practical amenity rather than an afterthought, according to industry observers. Financial considerations often weigh on property owners evaluating this kind of upgrade. Government incentive programs in Canada exist to help offset the cost of deploying EV charging infrastructure, according to regulatory sources, which can make the investment more accessible for commercial property owners in Mississauga. Realizing these benefits depends on installation performed to code. Ontario's Electrical Safety Authority sets licensing and safety standards for electrical contractors, and commercial EV charger projects must account for load calculations, circuit protection and documentation required by municipal authorities and utility providers. Skipping these steps can create compliance issues that surface only after a system is already in place. Crown Electric Ltd's licensed status allows the company to manage each stage of that process directly.

items.title: Hiked fines for illegal dumping and littering being considered in Mississauga
items.summary: Fines for illegal dumping and littering in Mississauga may soon be on the rise as the city considers beefing up enforcement and other measures to battle the ongoing problem. Current fines issued by the City of Mississauga for the dumping of household garbage and other items in parks, creeks and elsewhere range from $500 to $100,000 for residents and businesses. No specific penalty increases have yet been proposed as senior city staff were given direction Tuesday morning at city council to look into various ways to tackle the messy — and expensive — matter and report back at a later date. A motion adopted by council, which was brought forward by Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart, also tasked staff with identifying and responding to “recurring hotspots” of illegal dumping and littering across the city. ” City of Mississauga officials also raised the matter back in June, noting at the time the municipality had received 195 complaints to that point in 2026 related to the illegal dumping of various items. Dumped goods include car tires, paint cans, used furniture, construction waste, yard waste, propane tanks, household garbage and more. The city said it received more than 580 similar reports in 2025 and well in excess of 2,000 complaints over the past few years.

items.title: Trade War Response Takes Center Stage as Four Contenders for Mississauga Mayor Debate at Board of Trade
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, four candidates running for Mississauga mayor met on Sept. 25 for a debate hosted by the Mississauga Board of Trade and co-hosted by CBC News at Sheridan College's Hazel McCallion campus. CBC's Nav Nanwa moderated the event, which brought together incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla and Ward 2 Councillor Alvin Tedjo. Trade tariffs, transit and the future of Ridgeway Plaza were among the topics on the agenda. Asked how they would shield local businesses from the ongoing trade war with the United States, Crombie pointed to her record as former mayor, saying she helped attract more than $9 billion in investment and create tens of thousands of jobs. She proposed interest free deferrals on property taxes, lower business taxes, a guarantee that city suppliers get paid within 15 days, and a push to promote buying local while continuing to court outside investment. Damerla cited a Canadian Federation of Independent Business report ranking Mississauga 23rd out of 24 Ontario cities for ease of doing business, and pledged to move the city to first place to help tariff hit companies. Her plan also includes creating new jobs, considering property tax deferrals and encouraging residents to buy local.

items.title: Affordability, Transit and Fourteen Names on the Ballot Frame Thursday's Mississauga Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, four of the leading candidates for Mississauga mayor were set to debate Thursday night, moderated by CityNews reporter Mark McAllister, with election day set for Oct. 26. Fourteen candidates are officially running for the office, though recent polling points to a contest mainly between incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and Ward 2 Councillor Alvin Tedjo, with Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla still in the mix and a sizable share of voters undecided. Transportation was expected to be a central theme, with Crombie touting a transit platform that proposes extending the TTC's Line 2 subway west through Sherway Gardens into Mississauga's city centre, arguing residents lose too much time stuck in traffic. She has also pushed for stronger commitments from Metrolinx and the province to finish the Hazel McCallion LRT. Damerla built much of her campaign around fiscal accountability, renewing calls this week for the city to create an independent auditor general position to scrutinize spending and investigate complaints. Tedjo has leaned into affordability, unveiling a platform that includes a two year freeze on the residential share of Mississauga's property taxes and a permanent tax freeze for qualifying seniors.

items.title: City Partners With TRCA to Host Clothing and Electronics Drop-Off Drive for Circular Economy Month
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, October marks Circular Economy Month, an annual push to get residents repairing, donating and reusing belongings instead of throwing them out. The city notes that Canadians discard nearly 500 million kilograms of clothing and textiles every year, along with large volumes of electronics, even though roughly two thirds of those devices still work. To mark the month, Mississauga is partnering with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority's Partners in Project Green program to run a collection drive from Oct. 12 to 25, with drop-off bins for unwanted clothing, textiles and electronics set up at 13 city facilities. The city frames a circular economy as simply getting more use out of what people already own rather than replacing it. Beyond the collection drive, Mississauga Library is highlighting its makerspace programs, which teach skills residents can use to repair broken items, build gifts or create projects out of recycled materials. Officials note that a library card unlocks far more than books, pointing residents toward these hands on programs as one more way to take part.
